title: Scalar compatibility of the actual projective-line adjunction counit
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For a standing base $S$, set $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, $F_R=Rq_{*,R}$ and $G_R=q_R^*(-)\otimes_R^LR_P(1)[2]$. Use the actual adjunction $F_R\dashv G_R$ with counit $\epsilon_R$ and projection-formula normalization of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Let $\beta_q:T_SF_A\to F_BT_P$ be the fixed proper coefficient map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Let $a_K:T_PG_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_SK$ be the canonical tensor/pullback, Tate and shift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{et},A)$,
$$\epsilon_{B,T_SK}\,F_B(a_K)\,\beta_q(G_AK)=T_S(\epsilon_{A,K}).$$
In particular $a_K$ is the mate of $\beta_q^{-1}$ on these finite-Tor subcategories.

proof.text: Put $L_R=R_P(1)[2]$, $H_R=F_RL_R$, and write $t_R:H_R\to R_S$ for the normalized trace. Let $\lambda:T_PL_A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_B$ be the balanced twist comparison and $b=F_B(\lambda)\circ\beta_q(L_A):T_SH_A\to H_B$. Write $m_{U,V}:T_S(U\otimes_A^LV)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_SU\otimes_B^LT_SV$ and $e:T_SA_S\xrightarrow{\sim}B_S$ for the tensor and unit comparisons. The normalized adjunction gives $\epsilon_{R,K}=u_{R,K}\circ(1_K\otimes t_R)\circ\pi_{R,K}^{-1}$, where $\pi_{R,K}:K\otimes_R^LH_R\to F_R(q_R^*K\otimes_R^LL_R)$ is the forward projection map and $u_{R,K}:K\otimes_R^LR_S\to K$ is the right unitor. This is a formula for the actual counit. The twist is locally free of rank one, so its derived coefficient extension is the balanced ordinary one, and the exact derived scalar functor commutes with the shift.

proof.text: Use the geometric adjunctions $q_A^*\dashv F_A$ and $q_B^*\dashv F_B$, distinct from the exceptional adjunctions in the assertion. The square is the canonical isomorphism $q_B^*T_S\simeq T_Pq_A^*$. Its mate is precisely the specified $\beta_q$, because both are defined as the transpose of the scalar extension of the geometric counit. Its tensor compatibility is supplied by the monoidal composition comparisons for ringed-topos derived pullback: the two composites of coefficient change and geometric inverse image are the same ringed-topos pullback. Thus their comparison respects tensor products, unitors and symmetry. This applies to the identity geometric morphisms with structural ring maps $A_T\to B_T$, without assuming these maps flat. It also identifies the composite comparison on $q_A^*K\otimes L_A$, followed by $1\otimes\lambda$, with the specified $a_K$.

proof.text:
Apply the projection-mate square to the geometric adjunctions of step 2, with $N_D=T_S$, $N_C=T_P$, the tensor comparisons $m$ on both sites, $M=L_A$ and the base tensor factor $K$. Its hypothesis ComparisonCompatible is exactly the monoidal square verified in step 2. The result is the coefficient/projection square for the order $H_A\otimes K$. By lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection the forward projection map of step 1 is exactly $\pi_{R,K}=F_R(\sigma)\circ\mathrm{PF}_q(L_R,K)\circ\sigma$, with $\mathrm{PF}_q$ the counit-transpose map of def-kun-projection-formula-map (the map $P$ of the square) and $\sigma$ the derived tensor symmetries. Precompose and postcompose with these symmetries to use $K\otimes H_A$ instead; compatibility with symmetry from step 2 and naturality of $\beta_q$ give, after applying $F_B(1\otimes\lambda)$, the equality
$$F_B(a_K)\circ\beta_q(G_AK)\circ T_S(\pi_{A,K})=\pi_{B,T_SK}\circ(1_{T_SK}\otimes b)\circ m_{K,H_A}.$$
All maps here are the normalized ones: the projection map is the geometric counit transpose, and the coefficient map is its stated mate. In particular this square is not inferred merely from invertibility of projection maps.

proof.text: The scalar compatibility of the normalized two-summand splitting gives the trace equation $t_B\circ b=e\circ T_S(t_A)$. Here the $b$ of step 1 includes the same balanced twist comparison as that splitting statement. Thus the trace is compatible with this particular coefficient map, including its normalization by the Kummer class; no assertion about an arbitrarily chosen right adjoint or trace is used.

source.place: Charts: compatibility of iterated projective-line integration, actual counit at a complex; retained Step 7

proof.text:
The projection maps $\pi_{A,K}$ and $\pi_{B,T_SK}$ are isomorphisms by lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection, since $q$ is proper of finite type between Noetherian schemes (step 6) and $A,B$ are finite rings. Cancel these projection maps in the square of step 3 and substitute the actual counit formula of step 1. For $X=T_SK$ this gives
$$\begin{aligned}\epsilon_{B,X}F_B(a_K)\beta_q(G_AK)&=u_{B,X}(1_X\otimes t_Bb)m_{K,H_A}T_S(\pi_{A,K}^{-1})\\&=u_{B,X}(1_X\otimes e)(1_X\otimes T_St_A)m_{K,H_A}T_S(\pi_{A,K}^{-1})\\&=T_S\bigl(u_{A,K}(1_K\otimes t_A)\pi_{A,K}^{-1}\bigr)=T_S(\epsilon_{A,K}).\end{aligned}$$
The second line uses step 4. The third uses naturality of $m$ at $(1_K,t_A)$ and its right-unit equation $u_{B,X}(1_X\otimes e)m_{K,A_S}=T_S(u_{A,K})$. These are precisely the unit and naturality identities of the cited strong monoidal comparison.

proof.text: The standing base $S$ is Noetherian: a field is Noetherian and finite-type morphisms preserve this property by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian. Apply lem-sp-finite-coefficient-input-models to represent $K$ by a bounded flat constructible complex $P$; it also gives $T_SK\in D^b_{ctf}$. The exact inverse-image functor preserves the degree support, and ringed-topos pullback preserves its flat terms. Since $q^{-1}$ is exact, $H^i(q^{-1}P)=q^{-1}H^i(P)$. If $(\iota_k:Z_k\to S)$ is a stratification witnessing constructibility of $H^i(P)$ in the sense of def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, the base changes $\iota'_k:Z_k\times_SP\to P$ are immersions whose images $q^{-1}(T_k)$ partition $P$ into locally closed subsets, constructible by lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage; and $\iota_k'^{-1}q^{-1}H^i(P)\cong q_k^{-1}\iota_k^{-1}H^i(P)$ for $q_k:Z_k\times_SP\to Z_k$, which is finite locally constant on the base-changed trivializing etale covers. Tensoring $q^{-1}P$ with the twist, flat and locally isomorphic to $A_P$ by lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line, gives a complex of flat terms with cohomology $q^{-1}H^i(P)\otimes A_P(1)$, finite locally constant on the strata after refining by the trivializing covers of the twist; shifting by $[2]$ gives a bounded K-flat constructible model of $G_AK$. A bounded complex of flat terms in $[a,b]$ computes its derived tensor with any module $H[0]$ termwise, so it has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. This verifies that the coefficient isomorphism theorem applies at $G_AK$; the same argument works over $B$. All comparisons used above are natural. Precomposing step 5 with $\beta_q(G_AK)^{-1}$ identifies $a_K$ as the unique transpose of $T_S(\epsilon_{A,K})\circ\beta_q(G_AK)^{-1}$ under the exceptional adjunction over $B$. The defining mate bijection therefore identifies $a$ with the mate of $\beta_q^{-1}$ for $F_A\dashv G_A$ and $F_B\dashv G_B$.
